summary: The author attributes Placidus becoming a default to publishing convenience, Italian adoption and historical timing, rather than demonstrated correctness. British and French reception, Catholic influence and the later return of astrology are presented as a polemical historical account. The reusable methodological point is that inherited popularity should not establish a calculation method's authority. The page rejects inaccurate house systems as unsuitable for natal interpretation; it supplies no test design or independent accuracy evidence.
visual_observations: Historical references include the seventeenth/eighteenth and late nineteenth/early twentieth centuries.
No diagram or quantitative comparison.

assertion_candidates.proposition: An inherited default is not, in the source's method, sufficient justification for choosing a house system.
exclusions_and_limits: Source-method selection; historical assertions remain attributed, not independently verified.

name: IMG_4577.jpg
image_quality: Readable original photograph; full visible page inspected.
summary: Whole Signs is preferred as the default while the author also distinguishes it from invented house systems. Changing a house system changes cusp boundaries and may change planet houses, but does not change zodiacal planet positions. The size of the apparent change depends on the chart, with late-degree Ascendants specifically mentioned. The author disputes automatically equating Midheaven with the tenth-house cusp. Algebra examples illustrate that solvable mathematics alone does not demonstrate relevance to the interpreted subject.
visual_observations: Explicit negation: house systems do not change planetary zodiacal placements.
Example 5a=15 gives a=3; a longer algebra equality is an analogy, not an astrological formula.

assertion_candidates.proposition: Changing the house system alters house boundaries, not planetary zodiacal longitudes.
exclusions_and_limits: Natal chart comparison; does not approve the source's empirical correctness.

summary: The page describes Placidus as a temporal-hours method dividing diurnal arcs into thirds, influenced by tilt, season, latitude and birth time, and criticizes mirroring these into the lower chart. It contrasts mathematical elaboration with producing meaningful results. Two drawings explain the author's winter-solstice objection using daylight and chart proportions. These are evidence for the argument being made, not a complete implementation specification or an independent validation of the described astronomy.
visual_observations: Winter-solstice drawing labels diurnal arc 9 hours 24 minutes, 39.2% of the day, yet 50% of the chart.
Second drawing labels diurnal 39.2%, nocturnal 60.8%, AC east and DC west.
Lower text continues on next page.

assertion_candidates.proposition: The source criticizes mirroring unequal day/night temporal arcs into symmetric chart halves.
exclusions_and_limits: Explanatory critique only; source arithmetic/geometric conclusions need separate verification.

summary: The author criticizes unequal Placidus houses, interceptions and extreme-latitude breakdown, then differentiates Campanus spatial thirds from Regiomontanus equatorial divisions projected onto the ecliptic. Equal House is described as taking the exact Ascendant degree and repeating it in each successive sign at thirty-degree intervals. A worked wheel uses nineteen degrees throughout; the author separately gives thirteen degrees as a personal example. The absolute assertion that all systems must work for everyone is the author's stated standard, not an established accuracy finding.
visual_observations: Equal-House wheel repeats 19 degrees at twelve cusps and labels AC 19 degrees.
Regiomontanus described as twelve 30-degree segments.
Personal 13-degree example is distinct from 19-degree diagram.

assertion_candidates.proposition: Equal House repeats the Ascendant's degree as each successive sign's house cusp.
exclusions_and_limits: Description of a rejected alternative, not the approved Whole Signs algorithm.

summary: The author says Equal House initially seemed personalized but was rejected in practice. The central question is why an Ascendant or Midheaven should determine a house cusp at all. A symbolic association between zero Aries, the vernal equinox and zero declination is explicitly treated as symbolism. The page argues that houses should follow the planet's or universe's natural divisions and describes competing systems as human inventions. These are philosophical source premises rather than an empirical demonstration of those divisions.
visual_observations: Explicit symbolic qualifier accompanies Aries 0 degrees, equinox and 0-degree declination.
No figure, table or calculation recipe.
Right-side object does not obstruct the text being reviewed.

assertion_candidates.proposition: Symbolic resemblance between an angle and a house does not by itself justify using that angle as a cusp.
exclusions_and_limits: Source's methodological argument; astronomy claims are attributed.

The familiar pairings of these points with houses one, seven, ten and four are listed as positions the author rejects, with detailed alternative meanings deferred to a later chapter.

MC range is explicitly 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th, 11th or 12th.
No replacement anchor meanings are defined here.

summary: The source defines Midheaven as the meridian's intersection with the ecliptic and separates it from Zenith and from the Sun's highest daily position. It rejects attaching zodiacal or Saturn meaning simply to that geometry and emphasizes location and direction. The second section introduces an Elvis Presley comparison between Placidus and Whole Signs, explicitly choosing a birth time said to be verified and rejecting guessed celebrity times. The page introduces the case but contains neither the complete chart comparison nor external verification of the birth record.
visual_observations: MC and Zenith are explicitly distinguished.
Case-study premise says birth time verified; underlying documentation is not shown.
No chart drawing appears on this page.

assertion_candidates.proposition: Treat Midheaven as its own meridian/ecliptic point rather than a synonym for Zenith or a tenth-house theme.
exclusions_and_limits: Source geometry and interpretive scope; no independent astronomical correction inferred.
